stem:
Adeel looks at the diagram of a rectangular grid that is $7$ squares tall and $6$ squares wide. He wants the even-or-odd parity of the total number of small squares.

Which claim correctly decides that parity?

options.text: The total is even, because one side length is even.
Call the answer the label $7$, taking only the tall count.
Treat the parity as unknown until $7\times 6$ is fully multiplied out.
Say the even-or-odd decision is what creates the $7$-by-$6$ grid sizes.

teacher.key_rationale: A rectangular grid has an odd total only when both side lengths are odd. Here 6 is even, so the total is even. Naming 7 alone, insisting on the product first, or reversing parity as cause of the sizes miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as a 7-by-6 rectangular grid of unit squares with side counts labelled.
